summary:
Space Garden is an interactive 3D educational game developed by team Pilas N.A.S.A. for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Space Mission Design Game challenge.
Our project helps students and beginners understand how engineering decisions affect the success of space missions. Players design spacecraft for the Moon or Mars, selecting components while balancing mass, power, budget, communications, and scientific objectives.
Unlike isolated learning activities, Space Garden connects spacecraft design with mission operations. Players experience emergencies, solve role-based challenges, attempt landings, explore planetary surfaces, and receive feedback explaining the consequences of their decisions.
The game supports individual play and online cooperation for up to four players. Built with JavaScript, Three.js, and WebRTC technologies, it runs directly in a web browser.
By transforming complex engineering trade-offs into interactive challenges, Space Garden makes space systems engineering more accessible, engaging, and understandable.
details:
Project Overview

Space Garden is a browser-based 3D educational game designed to help students understand the engineering decisions involved in planning and operating a space mission.

How It Works

Players select the Moon or Mars as their destination and configure a spacecraft by choosing propulsion, structures, solar panels, batteries, scientific instruments, and communication systems.

Each component affects mission resources, including mass, power consumption, budget, and operational risks. The game evaluates these decisions and provides warnings when the spacecraft does not meet mission requirements.

After completing the design, players travel through space, respond to technical emergencies through interactive minigames, perform a landing, explore the planetary surface, collect scientific samples, and receive a final mission report.

Space Garden supports both single-player and cooperative multiplayer experiences with up to four participants. Each participant can take responsibility for piloting, engineering, science, or communications.

Innovation and Educational Impact

Our main innovation is connecting spacecraft design decisions with operational consequences and educational feedback.

Rather than presenting space engineering as isolated theoretical concepts, Space Garden allows players to experiment with trade-offs, experience failures, understand their causes, and improve their designs.

The game incorporates simplified engineering models, educational guidance, real NASA mission examples, and interactive challenges to make complex concepts understandable to beginners.

Technology

The project was developed using JavaScript, Three.js for 3D graphics, Vite for development and building, PeerJS and WebRTC for cooperative communication, and JSON files for mission configurations and educational data.

The game runs in modern web browsers without requiring specialized hardware.

Scientific Foundation

Space Garden incorporates NASA educational resources, planetary information, mission examples, and systems-engineering concepts. Some parameters are deliberately simplified for educational gameplay. The game is not intended to replace professional orbital simulation tools.

Future Development

Future improvements include more mission destinations, expanded orbital planning, additional scientific instruments, and educational validation with students.
